Story:

When I was at a prep school, I had a great maths instructor. I hated math, however.

One day, I was sitting there and finding the area of right triangles. I was having a hell of a time. This next moment changed my life forever...

He said, and I remember it well, "You know, David, that all you need to do is square the triangles, find the area, and divide that in half."

It was at that moment in time that I realized math was a language and that it was telling me what to do and what the problem was. I wasn't suddenly great at math. No, I'd suck for a long time to come. I had to unlearn what I learned by rote and approach it like one would approach learning a foreign language.

It was that moment in time when I realized, "Shit, it's telling me to do something. It can even be said in very different ways, like regional accents and preferences." I'm now almost 60 years old and one of my proudest moments was when that same teacher came to observe my dissertation defense. We are still fast friends.

The problem is money. She makes about 30k a year and I don't know how we can supplement that income. I was thinking about doing Uber or something like that, but I wanted to see if you ladies had any advice on things we can do to help make ends meet.

Never underestimate being thrifty. It's amazing how much you can reduce monthly expenses.

First thing I would do is get ride of debts, cut expenses as much as you can, and get a 3-6 months of expenses nest egg. It's worth removing that stress before she stops working.

My family always had family side jobs. Paper routes, window washing, snow blowing, lawn Care, or janitorial stuff. Helps the kids learn responsibility, handling their bank account, appreciating the value of a dollar, and can put a little extra in the accounts.

There's also part time or work from home jobs she can still do. Before adding even more to your plate, explore more options about reducing costs, finding a better budget system, stuff like couponing, improving your earning potential at current or new job, and finding ways for her and the family pull in a little extra.

It is easier to reduce your expenses than it is to raise you income.

If the family is carrying debt, you are going to have to prioritize eliminating it.

I'm the meantime, start fully accounting for all your outgoing expenses. There is probably a lot of waste in there but you need to know where so it can be eliminated. Things like buying your morning coffee out every work day can easily surpass 1k a year.

Be realistic about what the family actually needs versus luxuries. Do you really need disposable paper towels or would some reusable cloth towels make do with a little effort? Can you become a one car household? Thousands more in savings right there. Lots of things your family likes but can do without .

Learning to do things yourself is also great savings. Everyone should learn to make laundry soap. Searchvoat.co can help you search for older post on soap making.

Do you have specific areas where you know the family is struggling to be frugal?

I agree with these ladies. Cutting expenses and looking into side jobs she could do at home or a part time job that would not really take away from the family too much. I am given most of my kids clothes by my aunts but when I have to buy clothes I try to buy used. I buy most things used actually or on sale. Places like craft stores always have online coupons so if you need to buy something from there always check for coupons first.

Thank you for the good advice. I think the biggest frivolous expense we have is meals.

Because we are both working, we don't always have time to have dinner planned out. Most days I get home hours before my wife and trying to juggle helping with kids homework and making dinner, makes buying already made meals appealing.

That is one good reason for a wife to stay home so there is more time for meal making and planning.

That being said I know a lot of people have great luck with prepping all meals for the week over the weekend. That or doing a bunch of freezer meals once a week or once a month.
